title: Forensic Glass Fragment Analysis Lab
description: You are a forensic chemist analyzing glass fragments embedded in a shoe found at a crime scene. Examine the broken glass window and the shoe, perform refractive index measurements on fragments, run chemical composition tests, and match evidence to determine if the shoe's glass fragments originated from the broken window.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements a forensic chemistry lab for glass fragment analysis. Load GlassBrokenWindow.glb on the left side of the scene as the crime scene evidence window, and MaterialsVariantsShoe.glb on the right side as the suspect's shoe. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 2, 5) looking at the origin. Add ambient light (intensity 0.4), a directional light from above-right, and a point light simulating a lab examination lamp that the user can reposition by dragging a visible sphere handle. Use OrbitControls for camera navigation. Implement these interaction steps with parameter validation: (1) Click the shoe to zoom in and highlight 4 clickable glass fragment zones marked with glowing green rings on the sole area. (2) Click each fragment zone to extract a sample, which spawns a small translucent shard object near a virtual lab bench UI panel. (3) For each extracted fragment, open a dropdown to select a chemical test: refractive index measurement, density flotation, or elemental analysis via SEM-EDX. Each test must be selected from valid options only. (4) After selecting a test, a slider appears to set the immersion oil refractive index (range 1.500 to 1.600, step 0.001) for the Becke line test. Validate the slider value is within range. (5) Click a Run Test button that animates a brief glow effect on the fragment and displays a result value in a styled HTML overlay panel. (6) After testing at least 3 fragments, a Match Analysis button enables. Clicking it visually draws colored lines between matching fragments on the shoe and corresponding regions on the broken window, with a confidence percentage. (7) Submit a final forensic report by selecting match or no-match from a radio button group and entering a refractive index value in an input field validated to 3 decimal places. Display a styled results summary panel. Use a dark lab-themed background color (0x1a1a2e). Add subtle fog. All UI panels should use semi-transparent dark backgrounds with white text positioned via CSS overlay.
